checks.note: In signUpload, PutObjectPresignRequest signs only bucket/key/contentType — no Content-Length, checksum, or ETag condition — so the PUT URL accepts a replacement body for the full TTL; confirmUpload does not invalidate it, and signDownload/signedDownloadUrl mint unconditional GETs that never re-check the stored sizeBytes/checksum/ETag against the live object. (A bucket-policy mitigation is outside this file, but none exists in the code.)

CoachProfilePhotoEventListener.onStorageConfirmed does link any confirmed coach_profile object via updatePhotoUrlByUserId with no content-type/size/status check (lines 27-48), but the claimed consequence — unmoderated public serving of arbitrary blobs — depends on photoUrl consumers and the upload allow-list not shown here; the finding's required verification (grep marketplace/moderation for photoUrl consumers) cannot be performed with only this file.

confirmUpload checks head.eTag() only for presence and persistConfirmed stores request.checksum() verbatim; formatChecksum then re-serves it as "sha256:<value>" via toConfirmUploadResponse and findActiveObject, so an arbitrary client value is presented as a verified digest. The verification caveat (whether ReplicatedStorageService or audit/dedupe consumers trust StorageObjectDto.checksum) could not be run — those files are not in scope — but that bears only on downstream impact, not on the in-file mechanism, which holds as described.

FileStorageService.softDelete authorizes solely via fso.getCreatedBy().equals(currentUserLogin) with no ownerId or admin check, while signDownload, reconfirm, and assertOwnership all use the immutable ownerId. The login-recycling branch of the finding depends on registration/deletion code not shown, but the finding states it conditionally; the core mismatch is shown in this file.

saveStep5 does confirm the trigger: it calls coachProfileRepository.updatePhotoUrlByUserId(userId, req.photoUrl()) with no read of the prior photoUrl and no fileStorageService.softDelete (only deletePhoto soft-deletes). But the finding's own verification caveat — whether the GDPR/account-deletion path deletes file_storage_objects by ownerId (which would bound the orphaning) or only currently-referenced keys — depends on FileStorageService, CoachProfilePhotoEventListener, and the account-deletion code, none of which are in this file, so the "orphaned indefinitely / GDPR erasure misses superseded photos" consequence cannot be settled here.

matches.note: R1 identifies the same defect: confirm compares client-bound Content-Type via HEAD and never inspects stored bytes, allowing arbitrary content served as images.
R6 states that confirm-rejected (and never-confirmed) uploads leave S3 objects with no FSO row, uncounted by quota and never reaped — same defect and consequence.
R3 flags application/octet-stream and .bin (plus text/plain) in the default allow-list defeating the type gate — same defect.
R10 identifies free-text entity with only three owner-bound entities, letting callers mint keys under arbitrary entityId namespaces — same defect.
R5 identifies saveStep5's prefix-only check with no confirmed/active/ownership/type verification, allowing never-confirmed, deleted, or non-image keys as the public photo — same defect.
